make.name: Tesla
make.description: American electric-car maker founded in 2003, known for the Roadster, Model S, X, 3 and Y and the Cybertruck. The Model Y and Model 3 are its volume sellers; the Model S and X ended production in May 2026 and the Cybercab robotaxi and Semi truck entered production in 2026.

models.name: Model 3
models.description: Tesla's mid-size electric sedan, delivered from July 2017 and one of the best-selling EVs of all time. The heavily refreshed 'Highland' version arrived in late 2023 (US 2024 model year), with a new Performance model in 2024 and a cheaper Standard trim in October 2025.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: The original design, built 2017 to early 2024 in Fremont and Shanghai; Long Range and Performance packs grew to 82 kWh for 2021.

generations.name: Highland
generations.description: Major refresh with new front and rear styling, a new interior with rear screen, better range and refinement; deliveries began October 2023 outside North America and January 2024 in the US.

models.name: Model Y
models.description: Tesla's compact crossover, based on the Model 3 and on sale since March 2020; it became the world's best-selling car in 2023. The 'Juniper' refresh launched in 2025 (US 2026 model year) with new styling and interior; cheaper Standard RWD and AWD versions followed in October 2025 and February 2026. A long-wheelbase six-seat Model Y L is listed separately.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: The original design, built 2020-2025 in Fremont, Shanghai, Berlin and Austin; optional third row (7 seats) in the US.

generations.name: Juniper
generations.description: Refresh with full-width light bars, new interior with rear screen and ventilated seats, quieter ride and more range; launched January 2025 in China and as the 2026 model year in the US. 'Long Range' was renamed 'Premium' in October 2025.

models.name: Model Y L
models.description: A long-wheelbase, six-seat (2+2+2) version of the refreshed Model Y with a 150 mm longer wheelbase. Launched in China in 2025 (deliveries from September 2025), in Australia in March 2026 and in the US in July 2026 as a $61,990 Launch Series built at Giga Texas.

models.name: Model S
models.description: Tesla's full-size electric liftback sedan, built at Fremont from June 2012. It was facelifted in 2016 and heavily updated in 2021 (Plaid). Tesla announced the end of Model S and Model X in January 2026; the last Model S was built in May 2026, after a farewell Signature edition priced at $159,420.

sources.name: electrive: Final Tesla Model S rolls off the production line

generations.name: Original
generations.description: The launch design with a black nose cone. Rear-drive 60 and 85 kWh cars first; dual-motor 'D' versions and Ludicrous-era P85D/P90D arrived for 2015.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: April 2016 facelift replaced the nose cone with a body-colour front; new 75/100 kWh packs, P100D, and from 2019 the Standard, Long Range and Performance line-up.

generations.name: 2021 update (Plaid)
generations.description: New interior with yoke and landscape screen, new dual-motor drivetrain and the 1,020 hp tri-motor Plaid. Built until May 2026.

models.name: Model X
models.description: Tesla's large SUV with rear 'Falcon Wing' doors and up to seven seats, built at Fremont from 2015 (2016 model year). Updated with a new interior and the tri-motor Plaid for 2022. Production ended alongside the Model S in May 2026.

sources.name: electrive: Final Tesla Model S rolls off the production line
Cars.com: Tesla has discontinued the Model X; 2026 is its final model year

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version with Falcon Wing rear doors and dual-motor AWD on every car; Raven-era Long Range and Performance versions from 2019.

generations.name: 2021 update (Plaid)
generations.description: New interior with landscape screen and yoke option, new dual-motor AWD and the tri-motor Plaid; deliveries began late 2021 as 2022 models. Built until May 2026.

models.name: Cybertruck
models.description: Stainless-steel full-size pickup unveiled in 2019 and delivered from 30 November 2023, built at Giga Texas. A short-lived RWD model was sold in 2025 and a cheaper Dual Motor AWD arrived in February 2026. On 6 November 2026 Elon Musk said Cybertruck production will wind down around mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab.

models.name: Roadster
models.description: Tesla's first car was a two-seat electric roadster built on a Lotus Elise-derived chassis from 2008 to 2012, with about 2,450 sold. A second-generation Roadster was first shown as a prototype in 2017; a redesigned production version was revealed on 15 October 2026, with production targeted for 2028.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Tesla's first production car, a two-seat roadster with a 53 kWh lithium-ion pack; updated as Roadster 2.0 (2009) and 2.5 (2010), with a quicker Sport version.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Two-seat hypercar first shown as a 2+2 prototype in 2017; the redesigned production version (dual rear motors, butterfly doors) was revealed on 15 October 2026. Tesla targets production in 2028 at Giga Texas and has published only claims, not homologated specs.

models.name: Semi
models.description: Class 8 electric tractor unveiled in 2017. A pilot batch was delivered from December 2022 (first to PepsiCo); the updated production version with Standard Range (325 mi) and Long Range (500 mi) trims entered high-volume production in Nevada in April 2026.

sources.name: Electrek: first Semi off high-volume line

generations.name: Pilot production
generations.description: Low-volume pilot trucks built from late 2022 for fleet customers such as PepsiCo.

generations.name: Production version
generations.description: Final production design with a light bar, about 1,000 lb less weight, 800 kW tri-motor drive and MCS megawatt charging; built at Giga Nevada from April 2026.

models.name: Cybercab
models.description: Two-seat autonomous robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals, unveiled 10 October 2024. Built at Giga Texas from April 2026 (pilot from February) and used in Tesla's paid robotaxi service in Austin since September 2026; not sold to private buyers so far.

sources.name: Not a Tesla App: Cybercab production ramp

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Production version built with Tesla's 'unboxed' process; single front motor, NACS DC charging.

sources.name: Drive Tesla Canada: Cybercab EPA certificate

legacy_notes.note: Original (pre-Juniper) Model Y Performance; correctly marked previous generation. Price 52,490, 455 hp and 510 lb-ft are unsourced and not carried over.
Original (2018-2023) Model 3 Performance, but the row is marked available/current. It ended in early 2024; the Highland Performance (2024-) is a separate variant. power is null in the row.

'Small' 300-mile Semi is the 2017 announcement; it was never built in that form. Claimed on the 2026 Standard Range (325 mi). Battery 600 kWh, 1,000 kW charging and the 20 s 0-60 are placeholders/unsourced.
Cyberbeast: price 79,990 is the AWD price (Cyberbeast launched at 99,990, now 102,490); max charging 15 is wrong (up to ~350 kW DC); torque 10,200 is a wheel-torque figure.
Semi 'Large' (500 mi): claimed on the 2026 Long Range. Battery 900 kWh unsourced, torque 0 and 30 kW charging are wrong; price 180,000 was the 2017 promise (now ~290,000 quoted).
Model S Plaid is marked current; production ended May 2026. Charging 30 is wrong (250 kW); price 74,990 is stale (last 124,990).
Model X Plaid is marked current; production ended May 2026. Price 79,990 stale (last 129,990); vehicle_class 'Full Size Luxury Sedan' is wrong (SUV).
Labelled 'Standard Range (2021)' but its 272 mi / 57.5 kWh describe the 2022-2023 Model 3 RWD (LFP). Claimed on that variant.
Original Model 3 Long Range AWD; full_slug 'tesla-model-3-standard-range' collides with row 204 and is wrong. Marked available but ended early 2024; 333 mi matches no EPA rating (353/358 mi).
Model S Dual Motor AWD (2021-2026); marked current but discontinued May 2026. Charging 30 wrong.
Model X Dual Motor AWD (2022-2026); discontinued May 2026; most fields null.
Original Model Y Long Range AWD (2020-2025); not marked previous generation but should be.
'Standard Range RWD' at 260 mi is the 2024 Model Y RWD (original generation), not the 2026 Juniper Standard RWD (321 mi).

Foundation Series was a launch package on AWD and Cyberbeast, not a separate variant; this row's 119,990 / 2.6 s are the Cyberbeast Foundation Series, so it is claimed on Cyberbeast (duplicate of 19).
Cybertruck RWD 250 mi / 60,990 are 2019-2023 announcement figures; the RWD actually sold (Apr-Sep 2025) was the Long Range RWD: 335 mi EPA, 69,990. Discontinued Sept 2025.
Cybertruck AWD: 340 mi was Tesla's 2023 estimate (EPA 325); renamed Premium AWD in Feb 2026 when a cheaper Dual Motor AWD arrived.

Roadster 2nd gen: 620 mi, 200 kWh, 1.85 s and 250,000 are 2017 concept/Founders claims. The redesigned car was revealed 15 Oct 2026 with production targeted for 2028; the legacy image shows the 2017 prototype, so it is not used.
Original Roadster: price 80,000 is wrong (about 98,950-128,500); 200 mi range understated (244 mi EPA).

Model Y Performance (Juniper) row mixes trims: price 44,990, 327 mi and 75 kWh/455 hp belong to other versions. Actual: 57,990, 306 mi EPA, 3.3 s, 460 hp. Its image tes_my_perf.png shows the pre-Juniper Model Y.

'Standard Range Highland' mixes Highland Long Range RWD range (363), Performance 0-60 (2.9) and top speed (163) with the 57.5 kWh RWD battery. Claimed on Highland RWD (272 mi, 2024). The 2026 Standard RWD (321 mi) is a separate variant.
